source.text:
After any Orca upgrade the mechanics are re-witnessed against `orca skills get
orchestration` / `orca skills get orca-cli` — but the compact guide is a KERNEL, not the contract: enumerate `orca skills get <topic> --references` and load
each `--reference <name>` (`--full` on older CLIs), because the worker contract, recovery, and legacy-migration rules live only there (`skills.ts:50-58`).
pin-it owns that loop; hand-editing from memory is how it went stale twice.

children.assertion: skills get orchestration and orca-cli return installed topic guides

probe.procedure: Run orca --version; skills get orchestration/orca-cli/orca-per-workspace-env; enumerate --references and retrieve EACH --reference exactly. Compare returned reference inventory with saved full guide files. Retrieval proves guide availability only.
probe.expected_receipt: At exact installed version, establish this predicate independently: skills get orchestration and orca-cli return installed topic guides. Capture before/after authoritative state where mutation is involved.
probe.precondition: No extra identity; installed 1.4.200 CLI and every listed reference. Older --full compatibility needs its older executable.

children.witness_scope: Full version-matched guide retrieval and all listed references are inventoried; only guide availability/content, never proof of described mechanics.

**Refusals are typed codes** — branch on `error.code`, never exit status or stderr; `error.data.nextSteps` is the recovery text (older hosts omit it):
`task_not_found`, `task_not_startable` (+`data.unmetDependencies`, `data.retryOf`), `inject_rejected`, `nested_worker_depth_exceeded`, `consumer_fenced`,
`dispatch_inactive` are policy; `runtime_error` is the catch-all: "do not retry unchanged". `orchestration-dispatch-refusal-contract.ts:8` declares the first
three ONLY; the rest sit at their own sites, anchored per code beside POLICY_CODES in spawn_worker.sh (#302); recovery `recovery-and-cleanup:96-108`.

Nested depth probe must be coordinator-designed safe refusal path, with no accidental agent launch or global setting change.

  `consumer_fenced`, `dispatch_inactive`) branches the same way, carrying `error.data.nextSteps`.

  `worker_done` and `heartbeat` only (`message-send-handler.ts:51-58`); a `merge_ready --to @all`
  would fan out to every worker and put N writers on one BASE.

children.assertion: group heartbeat is rejected

probe.procedure: Validate recipient membership before group send; try worker_done/heartbeat group refusals; merge_ready group delivery across at least two owned recipients. Never use @all in current shared runtime because group expansion may reach unrelated workers.
probe.expected_receipt: At exact installed version, establish this predicate independently: group heartbeat is rejected. Capture before/after authoritative state where mutation is involved.
probe.precondition: Disposable runtime or coordinator-provided fully isolated worker recipient group with no parent/peer handles.

source.text:
BOARD: `check --wait --types merge_ready,worker_done,escalation` → append in ARRIVAL ORDER.
   `--types` is the WAKE condition only: the Delivery that comes back is the whole FIFO batch, every
   type in it (orca-dag-semantics.md).

children.assertion: types wake returns whole FIFO delivery

probe.procedure: Through its actual terminal create >50 synthetic messages; compare inbox/task-list/dispatch-show/check --peek/check --all/default/--unread read state; check --wait --types handoff; compare mixed FIFO batch, replay, ack boundary; wait >31s for two stderr keepalives. For brief specs use whitespace and >160 characters. Crash behavior requires isolated runtime, not current shared app.
probe.expected_receipt: At exact installed version, establish this predicate independently: types wake returns whole FIFO delivery. Capture before/after authoritative state where mutation is involved.
probe.precondition: Coordinator-provided ordinary shell bound to fresh scratch Run; synthetic status/handoff messages only. Prior owned fixture has been retired.

children.witness_scope: 51 synthetic status/handoff messages: mixed-type FIFO 50, identical replay, then one and empty. Already queued handoff satisfies wake; delayed wake and crash durability unproven.

Also on `create`/`edit`: `--timezone` (a cron with no zone drifts against the team's day),
`--missed-run-grace-minutes` (how late a missed fire may still run — past it the run is dropped, not
silently deferred), `--reuse-session` / `--fresh-session` (existing-workspace automations only;
prefer `--fresh-session` for missions, since a reused session carries the last run's context into a
run whose whole premise is independence), and `--host runtime:<environment-id>` to place the
scheduled coordinator on a paired Orca server rather than the mortal desktop — pass the id from
`orca environment list`, never the environment's name.

source.text:
`tasks.deps` (JSON array of task ids) is the dependency graph the runtime promotes against.
`parent_id` is a decomposition hierarchy that is empty in real CLI fleets **only because the
fleet never sets it** — `task-create --parent <task_id>` and `worker-start --parent` do exist
and do write it, validated to the same Run, and worker-terminal listing/attention queries read
it (`orchestration.ts:134`, `task-store.ts:32-36` at v1.4.199).

children.assertion: tasks.deps is dependency promotion graph

probe.procedure: Create good and bad parent dependencies plus multi-dependency child; reject missing/foreign deps and foreign parent; read parent_id and deps; complete only one dependency, then all; fail another. Compare task-list and scoped inbox before/after promotion. For failure circuit use three coordinator-supplied disposable Dispatch attempts, never simulated task-update failures. Legacy dangling deps require isolated imported legacy fixture.
probe.expected_receipt: At exact installed version, establish this predicate independently: tasks.deps is dependency promotion graph. Capture before/after authoritative state where mutation is involved.
probe.precondition: Scratch coordinator and two owned Runs; native helper only for actual Dispatch/failure-count predicates.

children.witness_scope: A single completed dependency promotes child; failed dependency leaves child pending at observation; parent_id distinct from deps. All-deps conjunction, forever and circuit behavior unproven.

`escalation`, `status`. `decision_gate`, `dispatch` and `handoff` are all valid `send --type`

existing ones to `status` (`message-inbox.ts:81`), and writes no `dispatch` or `handoff` at all.
`decision_gate` sat in the load-bearing list until #302 — not because the CLI refuses it, which is
what that issue supposed, but because the runtime has stopped producing it.

source.text:
What *is* real and load-bearing: `worker_done`, `merge_ready`, `heartbeat`, `question`,
`escalation`, `status`. `decision_gate`, `dispatch` and `handoff` are all valid `send --type`
values a fleet *could* write (`orchestration.ts:71` lists all nine); the runtime writes a
`decision_gate` only on the legacy direct-ask path (`legacy-ask-operation.ts:101`) and migrates
existing ones to `status` (`message-inbox.ts:81`), and writes no `dispatch` or `handoff` at all.
`decision_gate` sat in the load-bearing list until #302 — not because the CLI refuses it, which is
what that issue supposed, but because the runtime has stopped producing it.

source.text:
**`--types` is the WAKE CONDITION, not a filter.** `check --wait --types worker_done,escalation`
decides when the waiter wakes; the Delivery it returns is always the **whole FIFO batch**, every
type included (`orchestration.ts:112`, `orchestration/messaging-and-gates:19-22` at v1.4.199).

children.assertion: types controls wake rather than filtering delivery

probe.procedure: Through its actual terminal create >50 synthetic messages; compare inbox/task-list/dispatch-show/check --peek/check --all/default/--unread read state; check --wait --types handoff; compare mixed FIFO batch, replay, ack boundary; wait >31s for two stderr keepalives. For brief specs use whitespace and >160 characters. Crash behavior requires isolated runtime, not current shared app.
probe.expected_receipt: At exact installed version, establish this predicate independently: types controls wake rather than filtering delivery. Capture before/after authoritative state where mutation is involved.
probe.precondition: Coordinator-provided ordinary shell bound to fresh scratch Run; synthetic status/handoff messages only. Prior owned fixture has been retired.

children.witness_scope: 51 synthetic status/handoff messages: mixed-type FIFO 50, identical replay, then one and empty. Already queued handoff satisfies wake; delayed wake and crash durability unproven.

source.text:
A coordinator `check` returns the Run's oldest FIFO **Delivery** (up to 50 messages) and replays
that exact batch until `--ack <delivery_id>` — the mailbox commits the delivery before waking the
coordinator, so a crash between receive and process never loses mail.

source.text:
#   SP=<dir> [PROFILE=rw] spawn_worker.sh [--mark-ready] <task_id> <worktree_selector> <title> [agent] [effort]
#   agent ∈ claude|codex|cursor|gemini|grok|droid|opencode|omp|pi (default claude)
# Prints:  supervised: HANDLE=<h> READY=<state>, DISPATCH=<id>, and LAUNCH_EFFECTIVE=<json> when the
#          receipt carries it.  custom-argv lane: HANDLE=<h> STAGES=<csv>
#
# Agent × profile coverage (flags are Orca's own autonomous "yolo" args from
# `tui-agent-permissions.ts:6-33`, so workers never block on a prompt; anything else fails closed
# and needs WORKER_CMD):
#   claude/codex/gemini → ro + rw + danger
#   cursor              → rw + danger (`tui-agent-permissions.ts:21` maps cursor to `--yolo`; Orca
#                         has no read-only mode for it) — also one of the three agents that
#                         `--model`/`--effort` can target
#   grok                → rw + danger (Orca has no read-only mode for grok)
#   droid               → rw + danger (Orca appends `--auto high`); ro → WORKER_CMD
#   opencode/omp/pi     → WORKER_CMD. opencode AND kilo are actively STRIPPED of
#                         `--dangerously-skip-permissions` (`tui-agent-launch-defaults.ts:5-8`);
#                         kilo stays off this roster for the same reason opencode fails closed.
# rw and danger use the SAME non-blocking flag; danger only adds the ALLOW_DANGER gate + the
# ephemeral-sandbox requirement (sandbox-policy.md). worker-start's `--effort` requires `--model`
# (a provider model id the fleet does not pin) — the validated `effort` arg applies on the
# override lane's launch command; the supervised path takes the agent's configured default.

#   SP=<dir> [PROFILE=rw] spawn_worker.sh [--mark-ready] <task_id> <worktree_selector> <title> [agent] [effort]
#   agent ∈ claude|codex|cursor|gemini|grok|droid|opencode|omp|pi (default claude)
# Prints:  supervised: HANDLE=<h> READY=<state>, DISPATCH=<id>, and LAUNCH_EFFECTIVE=<json> when the
#          receipt carries it.  custom-argv lane: HANDLE=<h> STAGES=<csv>
#
# Agent × profile coverage (flags are Orca's own autonomous "yolo" args from
# `tui-agent-permissions.ts:6-33`, so workers never block on a prompt; anything else fails closed
# and needs WORKER_CMD):
#   claude/codex/gemini → ro + rw + danger
#   cursor              → rw + danger (`tui-agent-permissions.ts:21` maps cursor to `--yolo`; Orca
#                         has no read-only mode for it) — also one of the three agents that
#                         `--model`/`--effort` can target
#   grok                → rw + danger (Orca has no read-only mode for grok)
#   droid               → rw + danger (Orca appends `--auto high`); ro → WORKER_CMD

# ephemeral-sandbox requirement (sandbox-policy.md). worker-start's `--effort` requires `--model`
# (a provider model id the fleet does not pin) — the validated `effort` arg applies on the
# override lane's launch command; the supervised path takes the agent's configured default.
#
# NOTE: <worktree_selector> is a RAW orca selector.

path, tid = sys.argv[1], sys.argv[2]
d = json.load(open(path))
r = d.get("result", d)
tasks = r.get("tasks") if isinstance(r, dict) else r
tasks = tasks or []
by = {t.get("id"): t for t in tasks}
t = by.get(tid)
if not t:
    emit("not-found", 0)
deps = t.get("deps")
if deps is None:
    deps = []  # absent deps is the ONLY value that legitimately means "no deps"
elif isinstance(deps, str):
    try:
        deps = json.loads(deps)  # "" and garbage both fail here -> refusal below
    except Exception:
        deps = None
if not isinstance(deps, list):
    # Corrupt/unreadable dependency metadata ("", 0, {}, bad JSON) must fail
    # CLOSED, not count as "no deps".
    emit(t.get("status", "unknown"), -1)
unmet = sum(1 for dep in deps if (by.get(dep) or {}).get("status") != "completed")
emit(t.get("status", "unknown"), unmet)
PY
)
# unmet first, status second, one per line. `read -r status unmet` word-split them, so a
# status whose FIRST WORD is a dispatchable one was dispatched: `ready for review` read as
# `ready` (#298). unmet is an int and cannot carry a space; status can, so it
# gets a line to itself and nothing splits it.

GUIDES.precondition: No extra identity; installed 1.4.200 CLI and every listed reference. Older --full compatibility needs its older executable.
GUIDES.procedure: Run orca --version; skills get orchestration/orca-cli/orca-per-workspace-env; enumerate --references and retrieve EACH --reference exactly. Compare returned reference inventory with saved full guide files. Retrieval proves guide availability only.

VERSION.procedure: Run orca --version and record exact stdout and exit; do not infer authentication from the version string.

WORKTREE.precondition: Owned scratch worktree on this branch with inert shells only; teardown help before creation. Completed follow-up fixture was removed.
WORKTREE.procedure: Create with explicit parent-worktree and setup skip; inspect returned composite id/lineage; address it by path and id; set/read comment and workspace-status; close --worktree SELECTOR --all; list terminals; require clean git; rm without force or archive if unsupported. Restart durability is a separate isolated-runtime probe.

MAIL.precondition: Coordinator-provided ordinary shell bound to fresh scratch Run; synthetic status/handoff messages only. Prior owned fixture has been retired.
MAIL.procedure: Through its actual terminal create >50 synthetic messages; compare inbox/task-list/dispatch-show/check --peek/check --all/default/--unread read state; check --wait --types handoff; compare mixed FIFO batch, replay, ack boundary; wait >31s for two stderr keepalives. For brief specs use whitespace and >160 characters. Crash behavior requires isolated runtime, not current shared app.

RUN.precondition: Coordinator-provided scratch coordinator and two owned Runs; for unbound fallback a separate disposable runtime containing no unrelated Runs.
RUN.procedure: Bind A; create task A; bind B; create task B; switch A; compare task-list/worker-list explicit A/B and bound defaults, run-current/run-show; send synthetic Run messages and check corresponding bound mailbox. run-list/unbound global lists must execute only in disposable runtime so parent/peer state is not probed.

DAG.precondition: Scratch coordinator and two owned Runs; native helper only for actual Dispatch/failure-count predicates.
DAG.procedure: Create good and bad parent dependencies plus multi-dependency child; reject missing/foreign deps and foreign parent; read parent_id and deps; complete only one dependency, then all; fail another. Compare task-list and scoped inbox before/after promotion. For failure circuit use three coordinator-supplied disposable Dispatch attempts, never simulated task-update failures. Legacy dangling deps require isolated imported legacy fixture.

GATE.precondition: Scratch Run with owned ready task; native helper for original injected preamble, separate low-level helper for inject path.
GATE.procedure: Try missing task/question and both option encodings before valid gate-create --task --question --options JSON; read blocked task; resolve marker; read ready task; inspect regenerated preamble separately from retained exact worker-start or dispatch --inject original payload. Legacy injection uses versioned isolated legacy runtime.

ASK.precondition: Coordinator-provided owned worker and coordinator with writable IPC, allowed synthetic prompts, bounded runtime timeout.
ASK.procedure: Worker issues ask with CSV options and short timeout; read question/current task/DAG gates; let timeout occur; resume same message id; verify no duplicate; reply by id; compare worker return/task state. Test coordinator ask separately with an allowed recipient. Default/cap values need distinct timeout-boundary validation; a successful reply alone does not prove timeout behavior.

OBSERVE.precondition: Coordinator-provided helper with controllable idle/working/prompt states; absent/remote/restart conditions require separate fixture.
OBSERVE.procedure: Capture worker-list --run then worker-show --dispatch at each controlled state; compare projection fields, observation.status/agentWait (missing vs null), attention and literal nextAction argv. Trigger missing/stale status without killing unrelated agents; trust-prompt and remote cases require owner-controlled fixtures, never bypass trust.

START.precondition: Coordinator-provided idle native worker or explicit fresh-launch fixture, owned ready task and worktree; never dispatch another worker independently.
START.procedure: Coordinator supplies exact terminal or approved fresh launch. Start task with exact placement; record state/stage/setup/launch/effects/turnStart/prompt, then authoritative task/Dispatch/worker reads. For failures create specific missing task/unmet deps/inject refusal/timeout preconditions BEFORE start; distinguish task refusal from absent mechanism. Release/close all owned resources afterward.

LOW.precondition: Coordinator-provided separate low-level worker fixture; retained exact original injected bytes and request UUID; scratch Run/worktree.
LOW.procedure: Via actual scratch coordinator terminal create/use authorized helper and dispatch --inject --json; retain original text securely before sanitizing publication; compare prompt stages, unsupervised worker row, messages before/after, worker-stop/release effects and exact retry. Never substitute regenerated preamble for original bytes. Close explicit external terminal afterward.

REPLAY.precondition: Owned inert shell for no-resend proof; coordinator-provided real agent plus original exact bytes for wait-submit/turn evidence.
REPLAY.procedure: Send one inert command with UUID and one observable effect; try original UUID shorthand and text-without-Enter; retry with exact terminal/text/Enter/UUID and compare effect before/after. Separately use agent original dispatch payload and short wait-submit to observe accepted/unobserved timeout, then replay after turn evidence. Regenerated preamble mismatch is a separate negative control.

WAIT.precondition: Coordinator-provided TUI fixture with known ongoing work; shell exit waits already yielded typed timeout, not satisfied field.
WAIT.procedure: On known working TUI, terminal wait --terminal H --for tui-idle --timeout-ms 100 --json; record exit and satisfied schema. Then reach idle and repeat. Do not classify shell timeout as disappearance of wait API.

AUTH.precondition: Coordinator-provided pair of owned worker identities and scratch coordinator; tokens retained privately, redacted from receipts.
AUTH.procedure: Use valid active task/Dispatch/capability baseline then controlled missing outcome, wrong task, old dispatch, wrong sender pane and revoked capability cases against ONLY owned fixture. Compare typed errors and authoritative unchanged state; correct binding before retry. Nested depth probe must be coordinator-designed safe refusal path, with no accidental agent launch or global setting change.

MESSAGE.precondition: Scratch owned sender/recipient and active worker for lifecycle types; Windows fixture for PowerShell-specific claim.
MESSAGE.procedure: Send synthetic permitted type with subject, typed report-path/files-modified and valid task/dispatch binding; inspect stored payload. For merge_ready verify delivery and no built-in merge/status transition on inert owned branch. Missing subject / invalid JSON must be separately observed. PowerShell quoting uses literal inert JSON on Windows, no external messages.

MUTATION.precondition: Owned scratch Run/coordinator and per-verb request IDs; helper only for dispatch deduplication.
MUTATION.procedure: For EACH mutation verb in installed help, capture request-show absent, submit original valid operation with request UUID, replay identical argv, verify one state change and completed request. Pending needs controlled delayed owned operation. Do not generalize terminal-send replay to all orchestration mutations.

RELEASE.precondition: Coordinator-provided worker whose terminal is runtime-owned, plus external-terminal comparison; controlled cleanup failure on disposable runtime.
RELEASE.procedure: After explicit successful settlement run worker-release and repeat, inspect archive/output and exact process closure; separately retain, release_pending, already_released and release_unknown via documented controlled fixtures. Existing external helper only proves retained exit zero/idempotence, not owned terminal auto-close.

BROADCAST.precondition: Disposable runtime or coordinator-provided fully isolated worker recipient group with no parent/peer handles.
BROADCAST.procedure: Validate recipient membership before group send; try worker_done/heartbeat group refusals; merge_ready group delivery across at least two owned recipients. Never use @all in current shared runtime because group expansion may reach unrelated workers.

RESTART.precondition: Disposable second Orca runtime, independent coordinator A/B and owned worker; legacy database at exact supported contract transition. Current shared app cannot restart or adopt live parent Run.
RESTART.procedure: Record owned tasks/dispatch/heartbeat/failure/message state, restart only disposable runtime, re-resolve handles; compare persistence and stale-handle error. Adopt with new coordinator, verify old mutation fenced and worker preserved/questions rerouted. Legacy migration verifies actual imported rows/tombstone, not guide text.

OLD.precondition: Separately installed v1.4.199 executable and isolated runtime; this worker has only required 1.4.200 live target.
OLD.procedure: Replay accepted-but-unobserved start against exact older version and compare receipt. Existing v1.4.199 source witness remains source-only; 1.4.200 receipts cannot re-witness old binary semantics.

PROFILE.precondition: Coordinator-provided per-agent fresh launch fixtures with approved installed models, trust and host settings; current task forbids paid/remote/danger launches and global changes. Native read-only cannot use IPC on observed substrate.
PROFILE.procedure: Inspect exact host launch setting read-only, then coordinator runs allowed per-agent --model/--effort/profile matrix; compare effective argv with actual process and harmless permission outcome. Native CLI --help proves flag spelling only. Run doctor/launch inside disposable authorized host for danger lane. Missing credentials/unsupported IPC are preconditions, not absent APIs.

PLATFORM.precondition: Owned Windows PowerShell or Linux installation fixture, depending on predicate. Current host is macOS.
PLATFORM.procedure: On target OS inspect executable resolution then execute harmless literal JSON quoting/CLI help probe; record exact installed Orca version and platform shell. Do not infer foreign-platform behavior from macOS.

ENVIRONMENT.precondition: Owner-provided disposable provider account/recipe and paired runtime; explicit provisioning grant. No network credentials or paid/remote provisioning authorized in this unit.
ENVIRONMENT.procedure: Establish provider create/suspend/resume/destroy teardown, provision via vm recipe doctor, record plain/JSON/connect variants and warnings. Compare fresh unique pairing to cloned post-serve identity only in isolated owned hosts. Never snapshot or mutate current shared server identity.

AUTOMATION.precondition: Coordinator-provided disabled automation fixture isolated from current schedules, approved no-cost provider/workspace, and controllable clock for schedule/grace cases.
AUTOMATION.procedure: Establish automation deletion/disable teardown first; create disabled schedule against owned scratch workspace with precheck exit 1; run once and verify skipped history with zero agent/terminal/worktree creation. Positive precheck and schedule firing require approved coordinator launch; test cron/hourly/daily/weekdays/weekly/RRULE/timezone/grace/session separately; remote host requires paired disposable fixture.

RETIRED.precondition: Disposable runtime or independently owned unbound scratch coordinator; inspect exact alias source/help before any call.
RETIRED.procedure: Call retired orchestration run/coordinator-start/coordinator-stop in isolated runtime with state snapshots; require mechanism-level replacement/recovery receipt and zero scheduling effects. Do not call legacy stop against shared parent scope.

RESET.precondition: Disposable second runtime containing only synthetic tasks/Dispatches and explicit reset authorization. Reset is prohibited on this shared runtime.
RESET.procedure: Snapshot synthetic state, invoke orchestration reset only in disposable fixture, then compare erased state and retained filesystem. Current deny-hook test is repository policy coverage, never live reset proof.

SCHEMA.precondition: Read-only isolated runtime database schema at installed build; no parent task contents.
SCHEMA.procedure: Inspect sqlite schema and PRAGMA version for isolated instance, then store synthetic text payload/result via allowed CLI and compare types. Source schema or receipt JSON is not proof of installed storage type.

SENDER.precondition: Coordinator-provided unbound ordinary terminal in isolated scratch context; do not remove sender context on parent-bound calls.
SENDER.procedure: Through the owned shell run safe scoped inspection with valid sender, then remove only its sender identity and compare no_active_sender_terminal. Restore original environment; no parent Run reads or token impersonation.

classification_note: CURRENT means the exact child predicate at its stated fixture scope. Original broad record is never promoted merely because one child passes. UNPROBED/TODO and PARTIAL-TODO are unfinished work, not valid parked terminal classes. No evidence of mechanism disappearance or hostile identity authentication was established.
